title: Kick-Ass
edition: Matthew Vaughn’s 2010 theatrical feature starring Aaron Johnson and Chloë Grace Moretz
synopsis: Dave tries to protect strangers in a homemade costume. His intervention brings him into a feud between a crime boss and a father who has trained his daughter to kill.
verdictRationale: Dave risks injury to help a stranger who is being beaten. That act of courage gives way to a family revenge story in which a child’s skill at killing supplies some of the biggest laughs. Big Daddy’s death shows what revenge can cost, yet the climax rewards his daughter for carrying his campaign forward.
ageRationale: Adults only is the proposed guidance. A captive father burns to death during a rescue, and the film combines graphic injury with a child carrying out repeated killings. Teen sex and frequent strong language add to the concern.
reflection: Big Daddy passes a grievance on to Mindy as if settling it were her inheritance. Remembering a parent’s suffering can be an act of love. A child should also be free to grieve and to lay that grievance down.

themes.name: Courage
themes.evidence: Dave intervenes in a gang assault despite being outnumbered. This early rescue establishes why his example appeals to others.

themes.name: Vengeance
themes.evidence: Damon trains Mindy to avenge his family, and the pair’s feud leads into the final confrontation. Revenge shapes her upbringing and the climax.

themes.name: Violence and cruelty
themes.evidence: The father’s torture is frightening, while other killings by the child are choreographed for laughter. Both recur within the film’s main attraction.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: A school rumor that Dave is gay shapes his friendship with Katie until he corrects it. The score reflects repeated references in their subplot. Dave explicitly disavows the rumor.

warnings.name: Sexual content
warnings.details: The film depicts sexual activity between teenagers.

warnings.name: Language
warnings.details: Hit-Girl directs a very strong insult at a gang.

warnings.name: Violence
warnings.details: Dave and Big Daddy are tortured on a broadcast. Mindy reaches her father after he has suffered fatal burns.

warnings.name: Drugs
warnings.details: Katie asks Dave for help with a drug dealer. The gang’s drug operation becomes a target.

themeScripture.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
themeScripture.connection: Paul asks what good could still be done after an injury. For Damon, one answer would have been to give his daughter a childhood outside his feud.

patristic.author: St. John Chrysostom
patristic.text: He did not say, be not spiteful or revengeful, but required something far better.

biblicalParallels.title: Whose wrong must Mindy carry?
biblicalParallels.filmMoment: Damon makes his grievance against D’Amico the purpose of his daughter’s training.
biblicalParallels.reflection: Paul asks what good could still be done after an injury. For Damon, one answer would have been to give his daughter a childhood outside his feud.

questions: What makes Dave’s intervention in the gang attack courageous?
What responsibility does Dave have to correct Katie’s mistaken belief about him?
What could Damon have told Mindy about her mother without giving her someone to punish?
What changes when the assault on the two captives becomes a broadcast?
How does the ending invite us to feel about Mindy’s skill, and what has learning it cost her?

title: Kick-Ass 2
edition: Jeff Wadlow’s 2013 theatrical feature, 102m 57s UK cinema classification
synopsis: Dave joins Justice Forever while Mindy tries to keep a promise to her guardian. Chris seeks revenge for his father’s death, drawing the heroes’ families into the fighting.
verdictRationale: Marcus wants Mindy to have a life in which someone else looks after her. Dave’s father also takes a risk to protect his son. These are credible pictures of parental care. The film gives a teenager’s humiliating revenge on school bullies the payoff of a comedy routine, even as the loss of Dave’s father exposes the cost of retaliation elsewhere. The sustained invitation to enjoy cruelty weighs most heavily in this proposal.
ageRationale: Proposed for adults. The threat of sexual assault, bloody dismemberment and attacks on loved ones can distress viewers independently of how they understand the satire. A school bullying sequence also dwells on public bodily humiliation.
reflection: Marcus asks Mindy to imagine a future beyond the one her father trained her for. An adult who helps a child give up a dangerous role may have to stay beside her through the loss of the identity it gave her.

themes.name: Parental love
themes.evidence: Dave’s father takes responsibility for the costume, and Marcus tries to keep Mindy safe. The two households give this theme sustained weight.

themes.name: Vengeance
themes.evidence: Chris builds an organization around retaliation for his father’s death. His pursuit drives the conflict and reaches Dave’s family.

themes.name: Humiliation
themes.evidence: Mindy makes her school tormentors violently ill in public. One extended reversal turns their suffering into the joke.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: Insect Man introduces himself by explaining that being bullied for being gay moved him to defend others. This brief account of his motive supports a provisional 1. Check the feature for additional scenes before finalizing prominence.

warnings.name: Sexual content
warnings.details: The villain threatens sexual assault. A separate pool scene includes breast nudity.

warnings.name: Language
warnings.details: Frequent strong profanity includes a discriminatory slur spoken by a hostile character.

warnings.name: Violence
warnings.details: Fights show severed limbs and bloody injuries. At school, Mindy deliberately makes bullies vomit and soil themselves.

themeScripture.text: Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.
themeScripture.connection: Romans 12:21 gives families a question about these two responses to danger. Who accepts a cost himself, and who makes somebody else pay?

patristic.author: St. John Chrysostom
patristic.text: He did not say, be not spiteful or revengeful, but required something far better.

biblicalParallels.title: What protection costs
biblicalParallels.filmMoment: Dave’s father risks imprisonment to shield him, while Chris pursues the family of the person he holds responsible for his loss.
biblicalParallels.reflection: Romans 12:21 gives families a question about these two responses to danger. Who accepts a cost himself, and who makes somebody else pay?

questions: What future does Marcus hope Mindy can have?
What changes for Dave when his father takes responsibility for the costume?
Why does Insect Man connect his experience of bullying with defending other people?
What would repairing the harm at school require of Mindy and of the girls who bullied her?
How does Chris’s pursuit of another family affect the way he remembers his own father?
